question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=2{x}_{1}(t)-3{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-2{x}_{1}(t)+3{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform $L$ to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a system with variables ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}.$ In terms of the parameter $s,$ the solution of the new system is

${X}_{1}(s)=\frac{2(2s-3)}{s(s-5)},\,{X}_{2}(s)=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}L\{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)\}=L\{2{x}_{1}(t)-3{x}_{2}(t)\} \\ L\{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)\}=L\{-2{x}_{1}(t)+3{x}_{2}(t)\}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}sL\{{x}_{1}(t)\}-{x}_{1}(0)=2L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}-3L\{{x}_{2}(t)\} \\ sL\{{x}_{2}(t)\}-{x}_{2}(0)=-2L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}+3L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}\end{aligned}
$$

which can be simplified to the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)-4=2{X}_{1}(s)-3{X}_{2}(s) \\ s{X}_{2}(s)+2=-2{X}_{1}(s)+3{X}_{2}(s)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}.$

Rewriting the system in standard form, we get the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}(s-2){X}_{1}(s)+3{X}_{2}(s)=4 \\ 2{X}_{1}(s)+(s-3){X}_{2}(s)=-2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, from the second equation, we have 

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=\frac{-2-(s-3){X}_{2}(s)}{2}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(s-2)[\frac{-2-(s-3){X}_{2}(s)}{2}]+3{X}_{2}(s) & =4 \\ (s-2)[-2-(s-3){X}_{2}(s)]+6{X}_{2}(s) & =8 \\ -2(s-2)-[(s-2)(s-3)-6]{X}_{2}(s) & =8 \\ -({s}^{2}-5s){X}_{2}(s) & =8+2(s-2) \\ -s(s-5){X}_{2}(s) & =2s+4 \\ {X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{-2(s+2)}{s(s-5)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${X}_{1}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{-2-(s-3){X}_{2}(s)}{2} \\  & =\frac{-2-(s-3)\cdot \frac{-2(s+2)}{s(s-5)}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-2s(s+5)+2(s-3)(s+2)}{2s(s-5)} \\  & =\frac{2(2s-3)}{s(s-5)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=\frac{2(2s-3)}{s(s-5)},\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{-2(s+2)}{s(s-5)}.
$$
